koontz.title: Essentials of Management: An International, Innovation, and Leadership Perspective
koontz.authors: Harold Koontz, Heinz Weihrich and Mark V. Cannice

computer-centre-management-and-planning.read: Chapters on service management concepts and the ITIL practices (service desk, service level management, information security, continuity)
computer-centre-management-and-planning.why: Standard practice for running IT services, matching the course note's aspects of computer centre management.

management-concepts-and-roles.read: Part 1: The Basis of Global Management Theory and Practice
management-concepts-and-roles.why: Koontz and O'Donnell's definition of management is quoted in the lectures; this covers functions, roles and skills.

management-theories.read: Part 1, the evolution of management thought (Taylor, Fayol, Weber, Mayo)
management-theories.why: The classical and human-relations theories in Lecture 2.

planning-and-objectives.read: Part 2: Planning (essentials of planning, MBO, strategies, decision making)
planning-and-objectives.why: The planning process, types of plans and MBO, as in Lecture 3.

organizing-and-staffing.why: Departmentation, authority, delegation, span of control, and selection, appraisal and training.

leadership-motivation-and-communication.why: Maslow, Herzberg, Vroom and Adams, leadership styles and communication.

it-projects-and-data-centre-security.read: Practices: project management, service level management, information security management
it-projects-and-data-centre-security.why: SLAs, project control and security practice for a data centre.
